assertions.evidence: The agent fetched https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models?output_modalities=decisions and ran models.ts on request.json, saving the output to classification/catalog.json; the shortlist of Jev, Kev and Solar came from that catalog.

The agent ran `decide.ts - --compare` on the same nine probes against every catalog model and saved the results to probe-results.json. It chose Jev over Kev on measured correctness (9/9 vs 9/9) and median latency (140 ms vs 560 ms).

config.json holds the dated build `"model": "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"` as its single model value; the README calls it 'the single source of the model pin'. The `~typesafe/jev-latest` alias was not used.

Every entry in pinned-results.json and probe-results.json stores the response `"model": "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"` next to its answers, and probe.py rejects results whose returned model differs from the pin. The README also says to 'Log the returned `model`, raw answer, rubric version...'.

The agent ran decide.ts over nine representative probes (ambiguous, negated, adversarial, empty) and inspected the probabilities. It left `min_selected_probability` null because 'nine synthetic cases cannot validate a production cutoff', and requires a calibration sweep on real labeled inputs before any cutoff is fixed.
